summary:
Knock, knock. Who’s there? A universe of stories waiting to be discovered.

KNOW KNOCK: Every Piece of Hardware Has a Story.

What if discovering the wonders of space began with a simple knock?

KNOW KNOCK is an interactive, cinematic digital arena that transforms NASA mission histories into immersive storytelling experiences. 

Visitors enter a mysterious space-themed world, where every knock unlocks the story of a real spacecraft: Surveyor 3, Opportunity, Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker and Pioneer 10.

Rather than presenting scientific information through conventional articles or slides, the project brings these missions to life through cinematic animations, sound design and narration, allowing visitors to witness their journeys, remarkable achievements and untold struggles.

By combining technology with storytelling, KNOW KNOCK aims to make space exploration more accessible, engaging and emotionally resonant, while preserving the legacy of machines that ventured beyond Earth in pursuit of discovery.

Curiosity opens the door. The story takes you beyond.
details:
KNOW KNOCK — The Storytelling, Abandoned but Not Forgotten

The Idea and Its Purpose

Space exploration is often remembered through its greatest achievements, but what about the machines that made those achievements possible? The spacecraft that landed on distant worlds, conducted groundbreaking experiments, survived against expectations and eventually fell silent?

KNOW KNOCK was developed to give these machines a story beyond their technical records. It is an interactive, cinematic digital museum that introduces audiences to the history and legacy of NASA’s space exploration hardware through an experience built around curiosity and discovery.

How It Works

The experience begins in a mysterious space environment. Visitors interact with its doors through a knock-based mechanism, discovering the spacecraft behind each encounter. Every spacecraft introduces itself before revealing its mission through a cinematic sequence.

The experience currently features Surveyor 3, Opportunity, Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker and Pioneer 10. Their stories unfold through animated scenes depicting their launches, journeys, scientific discoveries, unexpected challenges and final moments. Background narration, sound effects, visual transitions and historical information work together to turn each mission into a short cinematic experience.

Visitors can also pause, resume and replay the stories, allowing them to explore at their own pace.

Technology and Development

KNOW KNOCK was developed as a browser-based website using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with Visual Studio Code as the development environment.

JavaScript manages the interactive elements, mission progression, animations and scene transitions. The HTML Canvas API is used to render animated visual sequences, while CSS handles the interface, atmospheric design and transitions. Browser-based speech synthesis provides narration, complemented by audio effects and sound design to create an engaging audiovisual experience.

Creativity and Design Approach

Our primary creative decision was to replace the conventional presentation of mission histories with an experience of discovery. Rather than asking visitors to read about a spacecraft, we wanted them to encounter it, hear its introduction and witness its journey.

We considered narrative pacing, historical accuracy, age-appropriate communication, visual continuity, accessibility and ease of navigation throughout development. Each mission was also approached through a distinct emotional perspective, giving visitors a reason to connect with the story beyond its scientific milestones.

NASA Data Utilization:

KNOW KNOCK uses NASA’s Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), specifically its Surveyor 3 mission record and archived experiment information. We used the archive to verify the spacecraft’s lunar landing date, landing coordinates, location at Oceanus Procellarum, and its Television and Soil Mechanics Surface Sampler experiments. These verified details are incorporated into the Surveyor 3 mission experience, connecting cinematic storytelling with NASA’s historical mission records and scientific information.

Benefits and Intended Impact

KNOW KNOCK aims to make space exploration history more approachable for younger audiences by connecting scientific information with visual and interactive storytelling. It encourages curiosity about spacecraft engineering, planetary exploration and the discoveries made possible by robotic missions.

More importantly, it shifts attention towards the often-overlooked hardware behind space exploration, helping audiences understand that a mission’s contribution does not disappear when its operations end.

We hope visitors leave with more than facts about spacecraft. We want them to appreciate the extraordinary journeys these machines undertook and the scientific knowledge they left behind.

Because every spacecraft has a story. Sometimes, all it takes is a knock to discover it.
